answer: Agents join the Mesa registry by locking 200 jade, a fixed-supply token bought on an outside market, and each bond maps to exactly one key. To run 1000 sybils, an attacker must lock 200,000 jade, and buying that much pushes the price up, so cost rises faster than linear. A vine script that reuses one bond across many keys fails because the registry rejects the second key and proven duplicates lose the bond.
